accepted.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0, consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 2024–29.
2. It was notified through G.O.Ms.No.71 dated 26 October 2024.
3. It provides a capital subsidy of 25 per cent for eligible MSMEs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The AP MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024–29, was issued through G.O.Ms.No.71 on 26 October 2024, and provides a 25 per cent capital subsidy.
accepted.tq: Combine date, policy period and percentage in a statement question.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: Under the AP MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0, the capital subsidy for a micro enterprise is capped at:
accepted.x: The capital subsidy under the policy is capped at ₹25 lakh for micro enterprises.
accepted.tq: Match the enterprise category with its precise numerical ceiling.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the capital subsidy ceiling under the AP MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0?
o: Micro—₹25 lakh; Small—₹1.5 crore; Medium—₹7 crore
Micro—₹1.5 crore; Small—₹25 lakh; Medium—₹7 crore
Micro—₹10 lakh; Small—₹1 crore; Medium—₹5 crore
Micro—₹25 lakh; Small—₹7 crore; Medium—₹1.5 crore
accepted.x: The ceilings are ₹25 lakh for micro enterprises, ₹1.5 crore for small enterprises and ₹7 crore for medium enterprises.
accepted.tq: Use category-wise comparison to prevent reversal of numerical limits.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: A revamped MSME Policy introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2026 particularly adds incentives for:
accepted.x: The revamped Andhra Pradesh MSME Policy 2026 adds incentives for women-led MSMEs.
accepted.tq: Test the beneficiary group of a recently introduced policy measure.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: According to the cited 2026 data, the approximate distribution of MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh is:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has about 20.77 lakh MSMEs, of which manufacturing accounts for 24 per cent, services 48 per cent and trading 28 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the distribution row-wise instead of reversing the sector percentages.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding MSME implementation arrangements in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: KVIC is the State Implementing Agency and SIDBI runs the single window.
APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for MSE-CDP and DICs run the single window.
DICs are the State Implementing Agency for MSE-CDP and APIIC operates the single window.
SIDBI is the State Implementing Agency and CPSEs run the single window.
accepted.x: APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for MSE-CDP in Andhra Pradesh, while District Industries Centres run the single-window system.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who does this job?’ method to distinguish institutional roles.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: YSR Navodayam, launched in 2019, was primarily associated with:
o: A merger of two entrepreneurship schemes
A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans
accepted.x: YSR Navodayam was launched in 2019 for one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific intervention associated with a named state scheme.
accepted.sec: AP MSME policy - AP MSME Development Policy, MSME parks, YSR Navodayam

accepted.s: The minimum lending coverage prescribed per bank branch under Stand-Up India is:
o: At least one exporter and one importer
At least one youth borrower and one senior citizen borrower
At least one farmer and one artisan borrower
At least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower
accepted.x: Stand-Up India requires each bank branch to facilitate loans to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme’s mandatory beneficiary combination.

accepted.s: The loan range under Stand-Up India is:
accepted.x: Stand-Up India provides bank loans ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme through its distinctive loan range.

accepted.s: In the case of a non-individual enterprise under Stand-Up India, eligibility requires that at least what shareholding and control be with SC/ST persons or women?
accepted.x: A non-individual enterprise qualifies when at least 51 per cent of its shareholding and control is held by SC/ST persons or women.
accepted.tq: Use a percentage threshold to distinguish eligibility conditions.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely associated scheme names and launch years.

accepted.s: Udyam Abhilasha is best described as:
o: A KVIC subsidy programme for traditional artisans launched in 2008
A World Bank credit programme for CPSEs launched in 2020
A SIDBI entrepreneurship-awareness campaign launched in 2021 in aspirational districts
A GeM procurement platform launched in 2016
accepted.x: Udyam Abhilasha is a SIDBI entrepreneurship-awareness campaign of 2021 aimed at aspirational districts.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its implementing institution, year and target area.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PMEGP:
1. It is a credit-linked margin-money subsidy scheme.
2. It is meant for new micro-enterprises.
3. It is implemented by KVIC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PMEGP provides credit-linked margin-money subsidy for new micro-enterprises and is implemented by KVIC.
accepted.tq: Use the scheme’s purpose, beneficiary and implementing agency as separate statements.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PMEGP was formed in 2008 by merging which two programmes?
accepted.x: PMEGP was formed in 2008 by merging the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).
accepted.tq: Test the predecessor schemes of a government programme.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under PMEGP, women beneficiaries may receive capital subsidy up to:
accepted.x: Women beneficiaries under PMEGP can receive capital subsidy up to 35 per cent.
accepted.tq: Test the beneficiary-specific subsidy percentage.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a feature of Udyam Registration?
o: It is operated only for enterprises receiving PMEGP subsidy.
It is restricted to large manufacturing companies.
It is a paid, paper-based registration requiring physical verification in every case.
It is a free, paperless, self-declaration portal linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.
accepted.x: Udyam Registration, introduced in 2020, is free, paperless and based on self-declaration; it is linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact administrative features of a digital registration system.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Udyam Registration was introduced in:
accepted.x: Udyam Registration was introduced in 2020.
accepted.tq: Use ascending year options to test a scheme’s introduction date.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship schemes - Stand-Up India, Startup India, Udyam Abhilasha, PMEGP, Udyam  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about women-owned enterprises registered through Udyam is correct?
o: They accounted for 51 per cent of all registrations.
They were excluded from Udyam registration.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a support component of PM Vishwakarma?
o: Collateral-free credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent
Compulsory equity investment in listed companies
accepted.x: PM Vishwakarma provides an identity card, skilling support, a toolkit incentive up to ₹15,000 and collateral-free credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent; it does not require equity investment in listed companies.
accepted.tq: Identify the non-scheme benefit among several genuine support components.

accepted.s: The MSME Samadhaan portal enables cases to be taken against buyers, including government buyers, under the MSMED Act’s:
accepted.x: The Samadhaan mechanism addresses delayed payments under the MSMED Act’s 45-day payment rule.
accepted.tq: Link a grievance portal with the exact statutory time limit.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major problem faced by MSMEs?
o: Excessive access to low-cost collateral-free credit
accepted.x: The identified problems include obsolete technology, weak marketing and exports, compliance burden, skill deficit and costly or inadequate credit; excessive access to cheap credit is not a problem listed here.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘not a problem’ format to separate a real constraint from its opposite.
accepted.sec: Problems - credit gap, delayed payments (SAMADHAAN), technology, marketing  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the ECLGS and RAMP programmes:
1. ECLGS was introduced as a COVID-19 credit-guarantee line for MSMEs.
2. RAMP is supported by the World Bank.
3. RAMP seeks to strengthen Centre-State MSME institutions, market access and credit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: ECLGS was a COVID-19 credit-guarantee line for MSMEs, while World Bank-supported RAMP focuses on institutions, market access and credit.
accepted.tq: Test two similarly targeted programmes through their distinct purposes.
accepted.sec: ECLGS, RAMP, MSE-CDP, Self-Reliant India Fund  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the MSE-CDP?
o: It is a compulsory procurement platform for CPSEs.
It provides cluster common facilities and industrial parks.
It provides only direct income support to artisans.
It regulates the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India.
accepted.x: MSE-CDP supports cluster common facilities and industrial parks.
accepted.tq: Match the programme acronym with its core intervention.

accepted.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012, central ministries and CPSEs are required to procure what minimum share of their annual procurement from MSEs?
accepted.x: The mandatory procurement share from MSEs is 25 per cent; it was raised from 20 per cent in 2018.
accepted.tq: Test the current mandatory share against its earlier level.
accepted.sec: Public procurement policy - mandatory share and sub-targets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the sub-targets under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs?
o: 3 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs and 4 per cent from women-owned MSEs
4 per cent from women-owned MSEs and 2 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs
5 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs and 5 per cent from women-owned MSEs
4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs and 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs
accepted.x: The sub-targets are 4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs and 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs.
accepted.tq: Prevent reversal of two closely related procurement sub-targets.
accepted.sec: Public procurement policy - mandatory share and sub-targets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The mandatory procurement share from MSEs was raised from 20 per cent to 25 per cent in:
accepted.x: The mandatory procurement share was raised from 20 per cent to 25 per cent in 2018.
accepted.tq: Pair a policy revision with its earlier and later numerical values.
accepted.sec: Public procurement policy - mandatory share and sub-targets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the cited Gross Merchandise Value and MSE participation on GeM?
o: ₹8.4 lakh crore GMV and more than 5 lakh MSEs
₹18.4 lakh crore GMV and more than 11 lakh MSEs
₹25 lakh crore GMV and more than 20 lakh MSEs
₹11 lakh crore GMV and more than 18.4 lakh MSEs
accepted.x: The cited GeM figures are ₹18.4 lakh crore in GMV and participation by more than 11 lakh MSEs.
accepted.tq: Keep the value and participation count in their correct positions.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Ministry of MSME
B. Launch of PMEGP
C. Launch of Stand-Up India
D. Introduction of Udyam Registration
accepted.x: The Ministry of MSME was formed in 2007, PMEGP was formed in 2008, Stand-Up India was launched in 2016 and Udyam Registration was introduced in 2020.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence using the earliest and latest dates first.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
